subject: Oceanography
title: Carbon Storage in Sediments
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Carbon Storage in Sediments.

hook.text: The ocean floor is Earth's largest carbon graveyard—dead organisms accumulate for millions of years.

buildup.text: Carbonate shells and organic matter settle to the seabed—burying carbon below layers of sediment.

discovery.text: Over geological time, this process forms limestone and eventually petroleum—ancient sunlight stored as rock and oil.

twist.text: Bottom trawling disturbs seafloor sediments and can release stored carbon—like plowing a forest.

climax.text: A 2021 study estimated trawling releases 1 billion tons of CO₂ per year—comparable to aviation emissions.

punchline.text: The seafloor locks away carbon for ages—until we drag nets across it.

quiz.question: How can bottom trawling affect climate?
options: It disturbs sediments, releasing stored carbon
